Q3_anchor_vs_change.reading: if the abs slope d grows with the anchor b (positive corr) and d/b is roughly constant, the glucose effect is multiplicative on the anchor

conclusion: Closed-loop observational data cannot identify the insulin sensitivity here. The homeostasis the loop enforces creates two killers: (1) glucose reverts toward target regardless of insulin (~45 mg/dL drop from BG 160 with zero insulin), and that reversion is collinear with IOB (corr 0.54, the loop doses by glucose), so the insulin term collapses when reversion is controlled; (2) at target the loop holds BG there, so almost no excursion exists to measure (few near-target 4h windows, and those that exist read a loop-suppressed value). The best per-user ISF at 100 therefore comes from tuned profiles or the cross-sectional K/√TDD cold-start, not from drop/IOB.
